reason: The accepted F1 contract pack cannot represent several security-relevant records required by the ratified D0 design. F2 is forbidden from changing accepted F1 bytes, so signing the current underbound runtime would overclaim conformance.

contract_stop_findings.conflict: The closed authority_anchor schema permits only the ten listed fields. D0 requires the intent to bind proposed event/database digests, expected committed anchor, old/proposed event heads, and requires the committed anchor to bind its predecessor anchor. Those fields cannot be emitted through the accepted additionalProperties:false schema.

The closed restore_event schema omits the pre-restore request/actor coordinates, old/new authority coordinates, replacement-owner locator binding, revoked/closed/invalidated aggregates, restored database digest, and restore-abort temporary identity/protection/disposition fields that D0 says each discriminated variant requires.

retention.set is a mutating F2 owner operation and D0 freezes a durable 7..365 day override, but the exact closed authority_meta record has no retention value/effective-from fields and no other one of the exact 16 tables provides a current retention-policy record. Digest-only audit fields cannot reconstruct the value.

After a durable restore plan closes the write gate and protected credential handoff fails, the 32-operation inventory exposes no restore-plan inspect/discovery operation. authority.restore.abort requires a restore_plan_id that a failed restore call has not returned, leaving the owner unable to invoke the ratified abort path without an unratified side channel.

implementation_findings_not_masked_by_co: Current backup and anchor records use field names outside the accepted closed schemas.
Current restore produces a hybrid database instead of publishing the fully qualified backup snapshot.
Current bootstrap omits durable OWNER_PROVED and the legacy LEGACY_REMOVED branch.
Current public final race check omits equality of authority_generation.
Current persisted policy reason_codes and activity metadata are SQL text rather than accepted JSON values.
Current stale-lock takeover does not bind deletion to the originally inspected file identity.
Current credential.issue advances auth_epoch and silently makes prior active credentials unusable.
Several frozen capacity and authentication-failure rate limits are not yet enforced.
Persisted page cursor metadata depends on process-memory page entries and cannot survive restart.

working_snapshot.note: The product worktree intentionally remains uncommitted for owner disposition; these bytes are not a qualified implementation.
